venue: Día de Muertos Festival / Short Run Comix Festival
headline: Coming up: Seattle Center's free Día de Muertos festival (Oct. 31-Nov. 1) and the Short Run small-press comix fest (Nov. 7).
blurb: Día de Muertos is at the Armory Food & Event Hall and is free; it includes altars, sugar skull workshops, performances and art. It began in South Park in 1998.

headline: Fast-rising Seattle hip-hop crew 4UST Collective played a live set for The Stranger's Noise Complaint series.
blurb: Led by MCs Webb Wavvy, D. Mikey and Tyler Soze, with producer Qreepz and a live band.

headline: Mudhoney started their first Australia/New Zealand tour in more than a decade on Oct. 16 in Melbourne. It runs through Nov. 1 in Auckland.
blurb: 14 dates, including Brisbane's Zed 51 Festival on Oct. 24.

headline: Hazmat Crews Swarm Rep. Jayapal's Seattle Office Over Suspicious Package
blurb: Hazmat crews checked a building in the 2000 block of 6th Avenue on Friday after U.S. Rep. Pramila Jayapal's Seattle office received a suspicious package; no injuries were reported and the area was cleared. Jayapal said it resembled mailings sent to members of Congress and election officials nationwide and called the effort an attack on democracy.

headline: Salon Revolt: 60+ Gene Juarez Stylists Stage 'Sick-Out' Over Pay Cuts
blurb: More than 60 Gene Juarez employees called in sick Friday, forcing appointment cancellations at salons across western Washington, in protest of a pay-scale change they say could cut pay up to 10%. The non-union workers want good-faith talks; the company said it respects its artists' right to be heard and leadership is meeting with staff.

headline: Pre-Dawn Gunfire in Burien Leaves One Man Dead, Another Wounded
blurb: King County deputies found a man dead at SW 130th Street and 2nd Avenue SW around 3:40 a.m. Friday, then were led to a second man with non-life-threatening gunshot wounds. No arrests had been made and Major Crimes detectives were interviewing witnesses.

headline: Fremont holds its first-ever Zombie Crawl tonight (Oct 17), with drink deals for costumed zombies at 10 bars and a Thriller dance-off at Fremont Social.
blurb: Saturday, Oct. 17 in downtown Fremont; the Fremont Chamber shared the event on Instagram.

headline: The second Seattle Trans Underground Film Festival runs Oct. 15-18 at Northwest Film Forum. It fills the gap left when TRANSlations ended after 20 years.
blurb: Programmed by Sophie Amity Debs and Kory Caldwell. Last year's first festival sold out nearly every screening.

headline: FBI 'Most Wanted Fraudster' Dragged Back From India Over $600K Food-Stamp Scheme
blurb: A 64-year-old Kent man who owned a Tacoma grocery store was extradited from India to face six counts of wire fraud; prosecutors allege he ran SNAP cards for set amounts, handed back half in cash and pocketed the rest. Authorities say he fled to Canada and then India after his April indictment; he has pleaded not guilty.

headline: Arrest in Arson That Gutted Ex-NFL Star Desmond Trufant's Luxury Venue
blurb: Tacoma police arrested a man Wednesday in a fire officials say was intentionally set at The Sunset Estate, the event rental owned by former Husky and NFL cornerback Desmond Trufant; the house was a total loss. Trufant told police someone had turned on the gas at the property the day before the blaze.

headline: Homelessness Agency's Hidden Hole Hits $17 Million, Report Finds
blurb: A consultant's report found the King County Regional Homelessness Authority left Seattle and King County with at least $16.7 million in previously unreported costs, largely from administrative overspending, plus $4.4 million in interest owed to the county. Officials say repayment could take years, and the agency's board will decide on accountability Nov. 6.

headline: Cyclist Killed in Foggy Dawn Crash; I-90 Ramps Shut for Hours
blurb: A car struck and killed a bicyclist on northbound Bellevue Way SE near SE 30th Street around 6:30 a.m. Thursday in dark, foggy conditions; police said the driver was not suspected of impairment. Both I-90 off-ramps to Bellevue Way were closed until about 11:30 a.m.

headline: Fall City Teen Accused of Killing Parents and Siblings Will Face Adult Court
blurb: A King County juvenile judge ruled a 17-year-old accused of fatally shooting his parents and three younger siblings in 2024 will be tried as an adult on five counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder. Prosecutors allege the killings were premeditated and that he called 911 and blamed a sibling.

headline: ICE Still Mining WA Driver Data: 356 Arrests Despite Sanctuary Laws, UW Finds
blurb: A UW Center for Human Rights study documents 356 arrests on Washington roads that followed federal agents querying Department of Licensing data, through pathways including the Nlets data-sharing network. Researchers say the state's efforts to restrict access have been ineffective and expect queries to rise.

headline: Judge Lets Boeing Door-Plug Victims Pursue Punitive Damages Fight
blurb: A King County Superior Court judge rejected Boeing's bid to block punitive damages in a suit by 47 plaintiffs over the 2024 Alaska Airlines Flight 1282 door-plug blowout. Plaintiffs argue Illinois law could apply to decisions made at Boeing's former Chicago HQ; trial is set for Feb. 1.

headline: Flash-Bangs and Chemical Munitions End Hours-Long Tukwila SWAT Standoff
blurb: Valley SWAT took a man into custody Tuesday night after he barricaded himself in an apartment in the 3700 block of Southcenter Boulevard, using distraction devices and then chemical munitions under a judge-signed warrant. Police say he faces first-degree burglary and felony harassment charges.

venue: Rosette, Death & Co., The Ink Drinker, Majnoon and others
headline: Seattle magazine's fall drinking guide points to a zero-proof wave: Rainier Beach's Rosette specializes in no-alcohol cocktails, and Death & Co., The Ink Drinker and Majnoon all list NA drinks.
blurb: Rosette (Rainier Beach) opened in 2025 and specializes in zero-proof cocktails, plus natural and biodynamic wines.

headline: Gunman Buys an Item, Walks Behind Counter, Kills Belltown Gas Station Clerk
blurb: A clerk was shot and killed early Tuesday at a gas station near the Space Needle; police say a heavy-set man in black made a purchase, went behind the counter and fired, apparently taking nothing. No suspect was in custody.

headline: Fake-ID Thief Accused of Grabbing Costco Gold Bars From UPS Drivers
blurb: Snohomish County prosecutors charged a 21-year-old student-visa holder with identity theft and theft, accusing him of using fake licenses to intercept UPS deliveries of gold bars, silver coins and jewelry from Mill Creek to Issaquah. Investigators put the alleged haul at about $380,000.

headline: Inmate Bolts From Work Crew by Puyallup River, Caught in Auburn Hours Later
blurb: A state prisoner serving time for robbery and burglary escaped a work crew near the Puyallup River in Tacoma around 12:30 p.m. Tuesday. He was found in Auburn about 90 minutes later.

headline: Heavens to Betsy (Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer) bring their first album in more than 30 years to Neumos Nov. 5. Genesis Owusu moved up from Hidden Hall to Neumos because of demand.
blurb: Heavens to Betsy, the Olympia duo, released 'Baby's Gone,' which the article calls a '16-track mission statement.' The show is 21+ and $35.

headline: SPD Lieutenant Demands $3 Million, Alleging Racism and Retaliation
blurb: Seattle Police Lt. John O'Neil filed a $3 million tort claim alleging racial discrimination, harassment and retaliation, saying officers resist his leadership because he is Black. The city previously settled with four female officers who accused him and former brass of harassment; the city declined comment.

headline: 50 Shell Casings at Kerry Park: Two Shot at 3:30 a.m. Street Party, Juvenile Arrested
blurb: Two men were shot near Kerry Park early Saturday and police recovered about 50 rifle and handgun casings; officers stopped a car with a rifle inside and arrested a juvenile on assault charges. Both men were in serious but stable condition at Harborview.

headline: Drive-By Getaway SUV Runs Red Light, Slams Into Sheriff's Patrol Car
blurb: After a Friday-night drive-by on Meridian near 136th Street, a fleeing SUV ran a red light and disabled a Pierce County sergeant's patrol vehicle; two 22-year-old men were arrested at a Fred Meyer lot. Deputies say they found shell casings and an open tequila bottle, and a gun tossed from the SUV was stolen.

headline: 2 a.m. Bar Brawl Ends With Stolen Car Plowing Into Four Pedestrians
blurb: Police say a large fight broke out behind a North Everett restaurant early Sunday, and a man took a customer's car and struck several people while speeding away. Four pedestrians were hospitalized; the driver crashed a block away and escaped on foot.

venue: Nightclub on the 5800 block of 4th Ave S
headline: A drive-by shooting in a South Seattle nightclub parking lot killed a 36-year-old security guard and wounded a 27-year-old woman early Oct. 11; the getaway car was found burning.
blurb: Police responded just before 1 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 11, to the 5800 block of 4th Avenue South (SPD South Precinct). Hoodline calls it a Georgetown nightclub; KOMO describes it as a strip club.

headline: Nightclub Guard Killed in Drive-By; Getaway Car Found in Flames
blurb: A 36-year-old security guard was killed and a 27-year-old woman shot in the leg in a drive-by outside a south Seattle nightclub just before 1 a.m. Sunday. Police found the suspect vehicle burning less than an hour later; no arrests were reported.

venue: Bar Vacilando (with Rione XIII, Rubinstein Bagels)
headline: Update: an inspection found the 15th Ave E building safe, but Bar Vacilando and its neighbors are still closed. Vacilando's last day was Sept. 26.
blurb: Seattle Met (Oct 9) reports the three businesses closed in September, reportedly because of a crumbling brick facade. A later inspection found the building safe, but they remain closed.

venue: Saanj Winery Seattle tasting room & social house
headline: Woodinville's Saanj Winery holds a ticketed grand opening for its Seattle tasting room and 'social house' today, Oct. 17.
blurb: Seattle Met's Oct. 9 news roundup listed the ticketed grand opening for Oct. 17.

headline: Scarecrow Video buyer Mark Steiner retired in September after 34 years, during which the catalog grew from about 1,000 titles to more than 156,000.
blurb: He started in 1992; Scarecrow was cofounded in 1988.

headline: Seven Men Busted in Aurora Avenue Prostitution Sting
blurb: More than 20 Seattle officers led by the Human Trafficking Unit arrested seven men ages 22 to 64 on Aurora Avenue N for prostitution loitering and patronizing. Only three lived in Seattle; several drove in from nearby cities.

headline: Bite of Seattle Case Wobbles: Bullet Didn't Come From Teen Suspect's Gun
blurb: Prosecutors told a judge a bullet recovered from a surviving Bite of Seattle victim did not come from the 15-year-old suspect's gun, after an earlier finding that it didn't match the three people killed. He remains charged with assault and unlawful gun possession, and a 'grey area' remains over whether he shot anyone.

headline: State Orders Seattle Crypto Firm Coinme to Pull Its Kiosks, Pay $2.5M
blurb: Washington's Department of Financial Institutions ordered Seattle-based Coinme to shut down its crypto kiosks statewide and pay a $2.5 million fine. A multi-state suit alleged weak accounting and anti-money-laundering protections; the company has until year's end to remove kiosks in seven states.

headline: Ferry Meltdown: Engineer Sick-Out Sidelines 13 of 18 Boats
blurb: Twenty-three engine room workers called in sick Monday, knocking 13 of 18 ferries out of service at points and halting routes including Seattle-Bainbridge and Edmonds-Kingston. Gov. Bob Ferguson demanded every vessel run by Tuesday morning; strikes by ferry workers are illegal under state law.

headline: A new Liquor and Cannabis Board rule on leasing liquor-licensed premises (2SHB 1701) took effect Oct. 3. A separate retail product-placement rule is open for comment until Dec. 4.
blurb: 2SHB 1701, Leasing Liquor Premises: final rule (CR-103) filed Sept. 2, 2026, effective Oct. 3, 2026.
outlet: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board

headline: Chastity Belt announced their sixth album, All My Friends, out Nov. 6 on Seattle's Suicide Squeeze.
blurb: The singles are 'To Decide' and 'Designs'; The Stranger also highlighted 'Pavement.'

headline: Northwest Film Forum began screening seven days a week on Oct. 5, the first time it has done so with a full paid staff, as attendance climbs.
blurb: Attendance rose 62% from 2024 to 2025 and is up 27% so far this fall.

venue: Halloween pop-up bars (Rob Roy, Navy Strength, Dreamland, Stampede and more)
headline: Seattle's Halloween pop-up bar season is in full swing, with at least nine themed bars running through Halloween and into November.
blurb: Pop-ups: Haunted Library (The Dressing Room by Can Can, through Nov. 1); Spooky Island (Rich Rich, through Oct. 31); Nightmare on Wall Street (Navy Strength, Oct. 1-31); Little Haunted Lobby Bar (Edgewater, Oct. 1-Nov. 1).

headline: Seattle's Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's US stadium tour after saying 'Free Palestine' onstage, and he answered with his own Free Palestine Tour.
blurb: He said 'Free Palestine' at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 4. Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft barred him, and Sheeran said the promoter made the call.

headline: Volunteer-run arthouse Grand Illusion, homeless since losing its lease, is taking over the shuttered Varsity Theatre and aims to reopen in November or December with daily screenings.
blurb: The Varsity, which opened in 1940, closed earlier in 2026.

headline: Doris, a 'super femme' bistro and cocktail bar from Angela Dunleavy, has opened at the old Salumi address on Third Avenue South.
blurb: Owner Angela Dunleavy named it after her great-grandmother.

headline: Suya Palace, a Nigerian bar-restaurant in the former Golden Roosters space, mixes suya skewers with 'sports and suds.'
blurb: The menu centers on suya grilled skewers.

headline: Hillman City's sake-and-jazz bar Sake Noire, from Quan Liang and Yael Silverman, is drawing attention for sake cocktails and Japanese-Italian fusion.
blurb: Opened in summer 2026. Seattle Met's Aug. 7 roundup says it opened in July.

headline: The Seattle City Council formally recognized Denny Blaine, the queer nude beach, as an LGBTQ+ landmark after a court ruled the park stays open.
blurb: Council President Joy Hollingsworth sponsored the resolution, which suggests a physical symbol such as a pride flag.

headline: Ethan Stowell's Cut Club pushes back on Seattle prices with a happy hour of $12 cocktails and $10 wine, at a time when its regular cocktails run $15-$20.
blurb: Happy hour runs 4-6 p.m. and after 9 p.m. Many dishes are $15 or less, with a $12 dish of the day.

headline: Visit Seattle says the World Cup brought an $889 million economic boost and $109 million in taxes, though some neighborhoods say they missed out.
blurb: $889M is below the $929M preliminary estimate but above the $846M March projection. About 20,000 jobs were supported.

venue: Head in the Clouds trivia, Hillside Bar, Neighbor Lady, Central Cinema
headline: Bar trivia is booming: Head in the Clouds, started by two Jeopardy! winners, now runs quiz nights at more than 30 Seattle bars.
blurb: Leah Caglio and Sally Neumann started it as backyard quiz nights in 2021. Most of the 30-plus events run weekly and use paper answer sheets, not apps.

headline: Phinney Ridge's acclaimed Khmer restaurant-bar Sophon appears to be permanently closed after the state revoked its business license over unpaid taxes.
blurb: The Department of Revenue revoked the license in early June. A window notice cited three tax warrants totaling more than $163,000.

headline: KEXP is exploring a second physical home: a music and cultural center with a rooftop venue in a landmark building at Haight and Ashbury in San Francisco.
blurb: The partners are SF Heritage and Blue Bear School of Music. The 1903 Doolan-Larson building is San Francisco Landmark No. 253.

headline: The Brudi Brothers, Seattle sibling buskers turned Americana act, will open for Kacey Musgraves at Climate Pledge Arena Oct. 26-27, their biggest stage yet.
blurb: George, Conrad and Johannes Brudi started busking in Europe in 2013, then played Pike Place and Ballard markets.

headline: Country Roads, a line-dancing country bar from the owner of Kangaroo & Kiwi, is set to open this fall in the former Shingletown Saloon space.
blurb: Owner Bradley Howe has run Kangaroo & Kiwi, a couple of doors down, for 25 years.

headline: WFLM Seattle, a group of midnight-movie fans, is finalizing a lease to reopen Capitol Hill's Egyptian Theatre by the end of 2026, with repertory films and midnight movies.
blurb: The owner is Seattle College. SIFF did not renew its lease in 2025, after a 2024 flood.

headline: Queer Bar reopened Sept. 11 under its new owners, the team behind The Cuff, with Drag Race star Sapphira Cristál and a return to seven nights a week.
blurb: Joey Burgess and Murf Hall sold Queer Bar to Scott Walent and Dustin Akers, owners of The Cuff Complex. The sale was announced June 22, and the new owners closed the bar after Pride for a refresh.

headline: Beth's Cafe, the 1954 greasy spoon, is back open 24/7, restoring a classic after-bar stop.
blurb: The diner reopened in 2023 with limited hours and has been extending them since.

headline: A slimmed-down, cheaper Bumbershoot drew strong reviews over Labor Day weekend. Death Cab for Cutie closed it in their first Bumbershoot set in 10 years, and Bikini Kill made their debut.
blurb: It ran two days, run by New Rising Sun. One of the two main stages was dropped because of Memorial Stadium construction, and there were no shows at the Vera Project.

headline: New York's Death & Co. opened its fifth bar on Sept. 3 in Pioneer Square's RailSpur alley, after about two years of plans and a delay from August.
blurb: It holds 80 people, with indoor and outdoor seating and a 12-page menu.

headline: Kay Redden of the label Den Tapes won The Stranger's 2026 Genius Award for Music, which comes with $10,000 and no strings attached.
blurb: Other winners: The Beacon Cinema (film), Chef Lisa Bi (food), Betty Wetter & TUSH (performance), Anastacia-Reneé (literature), Actualize Artist in Residency (visual art).

headline: A closed downtown 7-Eleven is now 'Inconvenience Store,' a free art show stocked with handmade items by more than 70 mostly local artists, priced from $1 to $10,000.
blurb: Curated by Lilia Deering and Mary Anne Carter, who made the 2024 IKEA-spoof show STÖR.

headline: Rainier Beach's new 31,000-square-foot skatepark, with a bowl and a 'lunar flow plaza,' is nearly done, and locals are raising $40,000 for a mural.
blurb: It sits next to the Rainier Beach Community Center.

headline: After the World Cup left town, Pioneer Square lost Collins Pub (23 years) and later Luigi's (closed Sept. 19), and Luigi's owner cited a 40% rent increase.
blurb: Collins Pub (526 Second Ave) closed abruptly in late July after 23 years. Owner Seth Howard also runs Draft Punk and Last Drop bottle shops.

venue: Glitter Paw Lounge, Marigolds, Good Bones Coffee (Here Today Brewery)
headline: Here Today Brewery is taking over the 121-year-old former Theo Chocolate trolley barn with a cocktail lounge, a tiny oyster bar and a cafe, all due this fall.
blurb: The owners are Chris Elford and Dave Riddle of Here Today Brewery & Kitchen.

headline: The Crown pub opened Aug. 12 in the former Dane/Schooner Street space, and burglars stole its safe six days later.
blurb: Longtime Ballard bartender Bob Hougland and his wife, Christine, serve craft beer, pub food and sports (per Seattle magazine).

headline: Shabazz Palaces' eighth album, It's a Style Sport, comes out Oct. 23 on Sub Pop. It is Ishmael Butler's first full-length since 2023-24's mini-albums.
blurb: 10 tracks; the lead single is 'Ahh World (I Won The Alpha Bet).'

headline: Neighbors Katy and Bryce are turning the longtime Oliver's Twist into a new cocktail bar, The Silver & Gold.
blurb: Oliver's Twist was one of the city's early craft cocktail bars and ran for nearly two decades.

headline: About 40 security staffers at Fokus Industries' Neumos, Barboza and The Runaway formed the Neumos Security Union and filed for an NLRB election.
blurb: They announced it at a rally at 10th and Pike on the eve of Capitol Hill Block Party.

headline: Single Shot owner Ruadhri McCormick pleaded guilty to keeping $1.4 million in payroll taxes withheld from up to 87 servers, bartenders and cooks. Sentencing was set for Oct. 5.
blurb: From 2014 to 2024 he withheld $1,027,362 from paychecks and did not pay more than $400,000 in employer taxes, for a total of $1,446,341.

venue: Pike Place Market, Pier 62, Seattle Center (open-container pilots)
headline: Seattle used a new state law to let people walk around with drinks at World Cup events and Pike Place Market. The law runs through 2027, and city officials want to expand it.
blurb: The 2025 law, sponsored by Rep. Julia Reed (D-Seattle), allows roaming drinks at fan celebrations and shared outdoor drinking areas.

headline: Pike Street cocktail lounge The Belmont reopened June 25 under the owners of West Seattle's Otter on the Rocks.
blurb: New owners Tanakorn Jitmongkonkul and Erin Wilbur added a refreshed cocktail program.

headline: Three men were shot outside Pike Street's Cultura nightclub May 18 after a fight that club security tried to break up; all three were expected to survive.
blurb: It happened around 1:10 a.m.; two of the victims were bystanders on the sidewalk.

headline: Sam's Tavern closed its Capitol Hill location after 13 years on the 'cursed corner,' following its Redmond and Bellevue closures.
blurb: Its final weekend was announced May 7. The bar was known for its moose head and dollar-bill decor.

headline: Capitol Hill Block Party moved to Aug. 7-9 this year as a 21+ festival with more than 100 sets at Neumos, Barboza and outdoor stages.
blurb: Featured acts: MUNA, Disco Lines, Wet Leg, Parcels, Magdalena Bay, Tinashe (DJ set), DJ Trixie Mattel, Zack Fox and Amber Mark.
